SIM-TICK-0a.hypothesis: Whether two rulings the owner gave in MOUSE-LOOK-0's court (2026-10-02) can be taken into the tick command without leaving the windowless proof — SIM-TICK-0a, an amendment to SIM-TICK-0, whose entry stands unedited (dc1dddf2): they are rules of the tick, so they are locked with no window, no clock and no Win32 input, before MOUSE-LOOK-0 puts a real mouse on them. (1) SENSITIVITY IS A TYPED CONFIGURATION EVENT. The owner's ruling: the keys are physical control bindings at the shell level, their effects are typed configuration events, and sensitivity changes take effect at the next tick and are themselves recorded in the session's command stream, so the session remembers the configuration transitions and not only the heading they produced. A sensitivity action that takes effect is appended to the session's log as one event of kind sensitivity, carrying the configuration after it (the multiplier and the step) and the tick it was applied at. It is a configuration event, not a world event: it has no witness and it is not folded — the head after it is the head before it — because the head is the worldline's (frames and content), and the same world reached under another sensitivity is the same worldline. The session owns the configuration as replayed state: it starts at multiplier 1 and step 88, and only a sensitivity event changes it, by exactly one legal transition (the multiplier one up or one down inside 1..64, or the step toggled between 88 and 1). A timed look's inputs must carry the configuration in force when it was applied, and the session's tick block the configuration at the end. A refused action (below 1, above 64) is still no event. This amends SIM-TICK-0's saved form: there a sensitivity action left no event and was saved only inside later looks. THE PHYSICAL BINDING under ticks, a pure map: PgUp is multiplier up, PgDn multiplier down, Tab the step toggle; mouse motion stays the look and nothing else. (2) HELD KEYS: THE TICK IS THE COALESCING BOUNDARY. The owner's ruling: keep HOLD-WALK-0's law and make the tick its unit — keyboard repeat frequency is input production, 64 Hz is simulation authority. A fresh press always acts and is never coalesced. An auto-repeated press of a key in HOLD-WALK-0's held set (W, A, S, D and the four arrows) is bound as that key's press, but only the first repeat in a tick: every later repeat in that tick, of any held key, is coalesced — counted and traced, never an event. A repeat of any other key (an edit key, a class key, Q, E, a sensitivity key, Esc) is ignored and counted. So a held key contributes at most one step per tick, 64 a second, however unevenly the repeats arrive. Nothing about a repeat is saved: a walked repeat's move is an ordinary move. Everything else of SIM-TICK-0 stands: the tick, the look once and first, the delta, the nearest cardinal, the fold, certification at save.
SIM-TICK-0a.success_condition: on every gate, windowless, through shell simtick-selftest: (1) configuration — the owner's sequence PgUp, mouse, Tab, mouse, PgDn, by key name, saves exactly a sensitivity event (2, 88), a look with inputs carrying multiplier 2 and step 88, a sensitivity event (2, 1), a look carrying 2 and 1, and a sensitivity event (1, 1), each at its tick, against a Python twin's re-derivation; the head after each sensitivity event is the head before it; the same looks reached by other counts under no sensitivity change save a different log and the same head; the workshop's sessionwalk verifies the file; a sensitivity event removed, changed to an illegal transition (two steps at once, a multiplier of 0 or 65, a step of 87), carrying no tick, or a tick block that is not the final configuration, is each refused by both verifiers; a crashed run's journal recovers the configuration from its journaled sensitivity events exactly — a change made after the last look is kept, and the next look uses it. (2) held keys — a fixed script whose presses carry their auto-repeat marks: a fresh press and a repeat of the same key in one tick (both act); three repeats in one tick (one walks, two are coalesced); repeats in successive ticks (one walks in each); repeats of two held keys in one tick (the first walks, the other is coalesced); a burst of repeats in one tick as after a slow frame (one step); repeats of Space, a class key, Q, PgUp and Tab (ignored: the edit, the strafe and the sensitivity change happen once); every press becomes exactly its registered outcome at its tick, no tick admits more than one repeat, and repeats = walked + coalesced + ignored; the same walk with each walked repeat typed as a fresh press and the others left out saves byte-identical data. (3) SIM-TICK-0's rows pass with script S's saved log now holding its sensitivity events, their expectations re-pinned on purpose and named; a tick session resumes with the configuration its sensitivity events replay to. (4) fence — the session's sensitivity event changes the configuration by one legal transition, folds nothing and writes no W, M or camera; the held set is HOLD-WALK-0's own; the control map and the accumulator's admission are pure; LIVE-INPUT-0's, LIVE-SESSION-0's and LIVE-AUTHOR-0's bindings and the window loop are unchanged; shell/win32.rs still reads no mouse; no renderer source changes.

MOUSE-LOOK-0.hypothesis: Whether a real mouse can turn the camera of the one live session through the locked tick rules — MOUSE-LOOK-0, the fourth rung of the owner's ladder: real mouse -> 64 Hz accumulator -> command -> the existing live loop. The rules are SIM-TICK-0's and SIM-TICK-0a's, unchanged and not proved again here; this rung adds only what they left out: the clock, the mouse, the capture, and the loop presenting a free heading. THE ENTRY (the owner's ruling): shell look-window on the host and shell look-selftest on the mock are the live editor with the mouse — the same loop function, session, journal and seal as shell live-window, with a tick source switched on; live-window, liveinput-* and livesession-* stay exactly as registered and pass no tick source. THE CLOCK: an input's tick is the tick of the microsecond at which the loop drained it (the window: QueryPerformanceCounter since the run began; the mock: its composition count times 13,333 us); a tick's command is applied at the first composition whose clock has passed the tick's end. THE MOUSE: Windows raw input (WM_INPUT), relative horizontal counts, as the device reports them; nothing else of the mouse is read, and pointer movement (WM_MOUSEMOVE) is never used as counts. CAPTURE IS SHELL STATE, never session state (the owner's ruling): while the window is in the foreground the cursor is hidden and confined and raw counts are admitted to the tick's accumulator; when it is not, the mouse is released and nothing is admitted; returning recaptures; a focus or capture change makes no session event of any kind — no look of zero, no pause, no synthetic input; Esc releases, then saves, then the reference recomputes. The shell owns where the mouse is allowed to speak; the session owns what the mouse actually said. THE PICTURE: at a free heading the loop presents the picture alone — the session's own render of that state by the production tread, the render its witness came from, rendered once, with no overlay; at an anchor heading it presents the composite as before. THE READBACK under ticks is sampled: the screen is read back at the first composition and at every 75th after it. THE LIVE SAMPLE (the owner's ruling): every 64th frame event at a free heading in the run is recomputed by the reference on a worker thread, off the loop; a mismatch ends the run refused and nothing is saved; a sample certifies nothing — the save still recomputes every free-heading frame. The 64 Hz tick against the panel's 75 Hz means some compositions repeat the picture before them: they are counted, not hidden.

MOUSE-LOOK-0a.hypothesis: MOUSE-LOOK-0a — an amendment to MOUSE-LOOK-0, whose entry stands unedited (60870497). It corrects one sentence of that entry, by the owner's ruling, and takes in what the first host run of shell look-window found. It is registered after that run: the run's counts (no mouse report, a span of 7, an end labelled closed) were seen first, and no condition below reads them. No rule of the tick, no rule of the loop and no renderer changes. THE TIMING LIMIT, CORRECTED (the owner's ruling and wording): a composition applies at most one closed tick command. span records the largest number of tick boundaries between consecutive compositions. A span above 1 therefore indicates the loop fell behind the tick schedule; it does not imply multiple commands were applied in that composition. MOUSE-LOOK-0's limit that a loop which falls behind applies several ticks' commands in one composition, and that the largest such burst is counted, is withdrawn: under that entry's own clock rule every input a composition drains takes that composition's tick, so it cannot happen. THE END OF A RUN: when the run ends, by Esc or by the window closing, the tick still open is closed there and its command applied, as the windowless tick run does at the end of its script; this is the one case in which a command is applied before the clock has passed its tick's end. On the host the presenter's window procedure destroys the window when Esc is pressed, in the pump that reads it, so the loop ends at that composition with the Esc's tick still open. A run whose tick run was ended by Esc is recorded as ended by escape in the saved file's live block, whatever the loop saw of the window; a run that ended because the window closed with no Esc is recorded closed. The mock closes its window at an admitted Esc press, as the host's does. THE WINDOW'S OBSERVATION OF THE MOUSE, EXTENDED: beside the reports it admits, drops and finds absolute, the window section counts every raw input message it receives, every one it could not read as a mouse report (with the size the last such read returned), and every relative report whose horizontal count is zero; a read counts as a mouse report when it succeeds, holds at least the mouse structure and names the mouse type, whatever exact size it returns. The observation is printed when the run ends and recorded in the live block. It is observation only: recorded, never ruled on, never an event, and nothing but the captured relative horizontal count is ever handed to the loop. THE SEALER'S READING: a session run under the tick source is described as that, with its look count, and is not said to have looked when it holds no look.
MOUSE-LOOK-0a.success_condition: on every gate, over the mock: (1) ending — a script ending in Esc ends at the composition that drains the Esc (that composition is not presented); the tick still open is applied as the run ends, so a key pressed in the same composition before the Esc is an event of that tick; the saved data is byte-identical to what shell simtick-selftest saves from the same inputs at their drain times; and both the loop's output and the saved file's live block say escape. MOUSE-LOOK-0's rows hold under the mock that closes at Esc, their compositions re-derived by the model. ADMIT-0.hypothesis: Whether a change to the world can enter the one session through a seam that reads untrusted bytes and gives them no authority — ADMIT-0, the admission seam, the first rung towards the design-event stream declared with LLM-BUILDER-0 (the owner's courts and review of 2026-10-03). The gate certifies the machine; ADMIT admits the world's changes. THE SEAM: shell admit --session S --proposal P, with a grant. The bytes of P are recognized or refused; a recognized proposal is checked against this shell, the saved session S and the grant; an admitted one becomes one ordinary edit event appended to S's log and sealed as a new session file by LIVE-SESSION-0's journal and seal. S itself is never modified. Windowless; one operation per proposal and one proposal per run. No model is in the tree, the gate is not invoked at content time, and nothing under verify/ is read by the seam. THE LANGUAGE (the owner's ruling: a line language whose accepted bytes are the canonical form, frozen as VRDNP1; a later language is a new version and never a change to this one) is exactly eight lines, each ended by one LF (0x0A), with nothing before the first and nothing after the last: line 1 'VRDNP1'; line 2 'renderer=' hex64; line 3 'bearing=' hex64; line 4 'parent=' hex64; line 5 'proposal=' hex64; line 6 'op=' and one of open, close, paint; line 7 'target=' and the target; line 8 'value=' and the value. hex64 is 64 characters of 0-9 and a-f. For open and close the target is coord ',' coord (x, then z) and line 8 is exactly 'value=0'; for paint the target is one of wall0, wall1, wall2, wall3, floor and the value is a colour. A coord is '0', or a digit 1-9 followed by at most four digits, and lies in 0..65535; a colour is '0', or a digit 1-9 followed by at most seven digits, and lies in 0..16777215, read as R*65536 + G*256 + B. No other byte is legal anywhere: no space, tab, CR, sign, leading zero, upper-case hex, quote, escape, comment, blank line, optional line, reordered line or repeated line. A proposal is therefore 327 to 337 bytes, and each typed proposal has exactly one byte sequence. proposal_digest is the SHA-256 of the exact bytes; nothing is normalized or serialized again. THE WORKED EXAMPLE, its eight lines in order, each followed by LF: VRDNP1 | renderer=e173d7c365dc91276e7976e3260d0dd5f73b486ee0486dfc124de4f4eac36348 | bearing=5cce76fcc31eeeef6635f2616acdeb7fbadb7cd365a20e23511676e7c0e4982d | parent=b02d86b948c4926b01978cb03b3b22bc4f0b013c2e93e3987f21a1ee23f6f37c | proposal=7454d41a3731607fba536bcfd045189eab260d37c8e15d65f8b2118ffd2c8da9 | op=open | target=7,12 | value=0 — 328 bytes, SHA-256 2e00fa35707be5294a3976f26274ec97991b9e294dce2983dddc3d2b91118789. THE ANCHOR (the owner's ruling: what a session already records; no program identity is minted): renderer= and bearing= must be this shell's renderer and bearing identities, and parent= must be the head of S as loaded. A stale parent is refused, always, naming both heads; there is no rebase. THE PROPOSAL ID (the owner's ruling) is the proposer's 64-hex handle, untrusted and recorded; an id already in S's admitted history is refused. THE GRANT (the owner's ruling: the admitter grants the scope) is given on the command line by whoever runs admit: the operation kinds allowed, an inclusive rectangle of cells for open and close, a set of tile classes for paint. What is not granted is refused, and with no grant everything is. THE EVENT is the edit a key would make — cell:x,z,. for open, cell:x,z,# for close, tile:CLASS,R,G,B for paint — validated by the session as every edit is, with one law added: a proposal that would leave W and M as they are is refused. Its head is the head that edit gives. THE ENVELOPE (the language, the proposal id, the digest, the renderer and bearing identities, the parent head, the resulting head and the grant) is recorded beside the event, in its journal record and in its saved item, travels with it through every later continuation, and is never folded into the head. ONE RECOGNIZER (the owner's ruling: parser unification): a proposal's bytes are read by one function of the shell and by nothing else. The workshop and the sealer never read the language; they verify the saved session — the event by replay, the envelope as typed values against the chain. REFUSALS are typed, and the first that applies is given, in this order: ADMIT-IO (the proposal cannot be read); ADMIT-SIZE (more than 337 bytes; the file is not read beyond byte 338); ADMIT-PARSE (the bytes are not the language: it names the first line that is not and what was expected there); ADMIT-RANGE (an integer outside its domain); ADMIT-PROGRAM (renderer or bearing is not this shell's); the session loader's own refusals for S; ADMIT-SESSION (S is a journal and not a saved session); ADMIT-ANCHOR; ADMIT-DUPLICATE; ADMIT-CAPABILITY; ADMIT-AUTHORITY (the session's validation, or nothing to change). A refused admission creates no run directory, no journal and no file and leaves S's bytes as they were: it is one line in the refusal log and one in the run ledger. A malformed command line or grant is the shell's usage refusal. A journal or a seal that cannot be written after the checks passed is LIVE-SESSION-0's refusal, as for any run, and leaves what that rung leaves.
ADMIT-0.success_condition: on every gate, windowless: (1) reader — the worked example is recognized and its digest is the registered one; each case of a hostile corpus given to shell admit ends in its registered refusal with exit 2, never a panic, an abort or exit 0, and leaves no run directory: every proper prefix of a valid proposal (the empty file among them), a repeated line, a missing line, two lines exchanged, an unknown key, bytes before the first line, bytes after the last LF, a missing final LF, CR LF, a space, a tab, a NUL, a byte of 0x80 or more, upper-case hex, hex of 63 and of 65 characters, a leading zero, a sign, a letter where an integer goes, a six-digit coord, a coord of 65536, a colour of 16777216, a value other than 0 for open, an unknown operation, an unknown class, a file of 338 bytes and a file of a megabyte; and in process (shell admit-selftest), over every single-byte substitution, deletion and insertion of three valid proposals, one per operation, each mutant is either refused or recognized as a proposal whose emission is the mutant byte for byte, so no proposal has a second spelling. (2) single parser — an independent recognizer written in Python inside the gate, a test oracle and nothing else, gives the same verdict, the same refusal and the same typed fields as the shell on every input of (1); and by source, a proposal's bytes are read in one function of shell/admit.rs, the workshop and verify/livesession.py contain no reader of the language, and both take the envelope as typed values of the saved form. (3) anchor — a proposal whose parent is not S's head is refused ADMIT-ANCHOR naming both heads; one whose renderer or bearing is not this shell's is refused ADMIT-PROGRAM; a journal given as S is refused ADMIT-SESSION; each leaves nothing. (4) capability — with no grant a valid proposal is refused ADMIT-CAPABILITY; an operation kind not granted, a cell outside the granted rectangle and a class not granted are each refused ADMIT-CAPABILITY; inside the grant, a cell outside the level, a border cell opened and a proposal that changes nothing are each refused ADMIT-AUTHORITY; each leaves nothing. (5) idempotency — a proposal admitted to S gives a child S'; the same bytes offered to S' are refused ADMIT-ANCHOR; a proposal with the same id and S''s head as its parent is refused ADMIT-DUPLICATE; the same bytes admitted again to the untouched S give a child with the first child's head, content and admitted item. (6) crash — a shell admit-selftest run is ended (exit 70, nothing after it runs) at each of eight points: the bytes read; the proposal recognized; every check passed; the run's journal opened with the parent's events; the admitted event's record torn half-way; that record flushed; the temporary saved file written and flushed; the saved file moved into place. After each, S's bytes are unchanged; after the first three no run directory exists; what the run left after the fourth and fifth loads through the shell's loader to exactly S's head, and after the last three to exactly the child's head with its envelope intact; nothing loads to any other head, and no state holds the event without its envelope or the envelope without its event. (7) replay — for each operation the child's head, content and event (spec and witness) are those of the same edit made by a key in the live editor's mock from the same parent; the workshop's sessionwalk verifies the child without the shell, replaying from the base; verify/livesession.py checks it, and its record cites this entry and counts the admitted events; a saved file, resealed, whose envelope names a parent or a resulting head that is not the chain's, a language that is not VRDNP1, an id or digest that is not 64 lower-case hex, an event that is not an edit, or a proposal id twice, is refused by the shell, the workshop and the sealer; the child continued by keys keeps the envelope byte for byte. (8) fence — shell/admit.rs spawns no process, opens no socket and reads nothing under verify/; a proposal's bytes reach the recognizer and the digest and nothing else; the commands and rows of the earlier rungs are as registered, any pin moved on purpose listed; the text of the saved form's JSON reader in shell/playback.rs, workshop/sessionwalk.rs and workshop/session.rs is untouched; kernel sources are unchanged; the LATENCY-0 prefix is intact. Off the gate, on the owner's host: shell admit on a session sealed there, the child verified by the workshop and sealed by verify/livesession.py citing this entry.
ADMIT-0.failure_condition: a proposal's bytes reaching anything but the one recognizer and the digest; a second reader of the language in the shell, the workshop or the sealer, or the Python oracle used anywhere but its row; a recognized proposal with a second spelling; a panic, an abort or an uncoded exit on any input; a refused admission that leaves a run directory, a journal or a file, or changes S; a stale anchor admitted, rebased or merged; an admitted event whose head is not the head of the same edit made by a key; an envelope folded into the head, separated from its event or dropped by a continuation; an operation outside the grant admitted, or a grant taken from the proposal; the gate, or anything under verify/, invoked or read at content time; a model, a network connection or a spawned process in the seam; any text of a proposal interpreted beyond its eight registered lines; VRDNP1 changed after this registration in any byte it accepts or refuses (a change is a new language version); the saved form's JSON reader hardened or its text altered here (that is READER-COURT-0, after this rung); a rule or the behaviour of an earlier rung changed; a claim that a model can write a proposal worth admitting, or any safety claim about a system that includes a model; a durability claim under power loss; kernel sources modified; the LATENCY-0 instrument altered (its text must remain a byte-exact prefix of shell/win32.rs).
interpretation_limits: no model is in the tree and none wrote a proposal on the gate: the gate's proposals are written by the gate, and the host's by the owner or by whatever he uses outside the tree; nothing here shows that a model can write a useful proposal, and no safety property of a system that includes a model is claimed

the vocabulary is today's: one cell opened or closed, one tile class painted; there are no regions, terrain, heights, structures or named objects, and VRDNP1 is frozen with this vocabulary — a larger one is a new language version, earned where the authority is earned
one operation per proposal and one proposal per run: there is no batch, so nothing is shown about a batch's atomicity

the envelope is a record written by the admitting shell; the seal is a hash and not a signature, so a saved file cannot prove which program wrote it: the verifiers check an envelope's parent, resulting head, language and form against the chain, and its digest, id, identities and grant are records nothing in a saved file can check; the proposal's bytes are not kept

the review's parse, depth, duplicate-key, unknown-field and schema refusals are one refusal here, ADMIT-PARSE with the line and what was expected: the language has no nesting, and a field occurs once at its registered position, so those cases are not distinct

the crash court ends the process at eight registered points; it shows what a restart finds after the process dies at those points, not at every instruction and not after a power loss — durability under power loss rests on the platform's flush and rename, as LIVE-SESSION-0's does, and is not measured
the seam is per saved session: the same bytes admitted again to the untouched parent file make a second child with the same head, and nothing global records what was admitted where
the grant is the command line of whoever runs admit: it bounds what one run may admit and authenticates nobody
the proposal id is the proposer's and is unique only within one session's admitted history
the hostile corpus is the registered cases and the single-byte neighbourhood of three valid proposals; agreement with the Python oracle is shown on that corpus, not on every byte string
the renderer and bearing identities are digests of sources compiled into the shell: a proposal written for one build is refused by another even where the edit would mean the same

the saved form's JSON reader is the one observed on 2026-10-03 to disagree with the sealer's on hostile bytes; the seam reads S through it after the seal check, and that disagreement is closed in READER-COURT-0, not here

the save recomputes every free-heading frame of the whole log by the reference at each admission, so an admission's cost grows with the session; nothing is measured about it, and no throughput, latency or feel claim is made

READER-COURT-0.hypothesis: Whether everything the tree saves and reads back can be read by one language, with every reader giving one verdict — READER-COURT-0, the rung after ADMIT-0 by the owner's order (his courts of 2026-10-04). ADMIT-0 made a new language with one reader; this rung hardens the old one. The saved-form reader is not a general JSON reader. It is a reader for Verðandi's own persisted language. THE LANGUAGE (the owner's ruling: the bounded saved-form language the tree's registered writers are permitted to emit; strict RFC 8259 rejected, canonical bytes rejected; corpus establishes coverage, the writer contract establishes the language). A DOCUMENT is one object followed by exactly one LF (0x0A), with nothing before the object and nothing after the LF. A PAYLOAD (a journal record's) is one object and nothing else. A value is an object, an array, a string, an integer, true, false or null. Between tokens there may be any run of spaces (0x20) and LFs and nothing else: the three writers share a data language and three layouts, not one serialization. An object's names are strings and no name occurs twice in it; an object or an array may be empty. Objects and arrays nest at most SEVEN deep. The count is of the objects and arrays open at once, the root object counted as the first; a string, an integer, true, false or null opens no level. Seven is one number in three places: the deepest shape a registered writer emits (a sealed measurement record), the deepest the readers accept, and the deepest the court tests — six levels and seven are accepted, and the bracket or brace that would open an eighth is refused at its own offset. The writers that re-emit what they are given have no bound of their own and take this one. AN INTEGER is '0', or an optional '-' and a digit 1-9 followed by digits, in -9223372036854775808..9223372036854775807 (the owner's ruling: signed 64-bit is the format's law): no leading zero, no minus zero, no fraction, no exponent. A STRING is a quote, its characters, a quote. A character is written raw in well-formed UTF-8 (no overlong form, no surrogate, nothing past U+10FFFF) when it is U+0020 or above and is neither the quote nor the backslash; the quote and the backslash are written \" and \\; U+0008, U+000C, U+000A, U+000D and U+0009 are written \b \f \n \r \t; every other character below U+0020 is written \u00XX with XX in lower-case hex. Nothing else is a string: no \/, no \u escape of any other character, no upper-case hex, no raw control character (the owner's ruling: one spelling, RECORD-0's canonical one; the workshop's writer, which wrote \u0008 and \u000c, is aligned to it). So every string has one byte form and two names are equal exactly when their bytes are. THE VERDICT on any bytes is ACCEPTED with a typed value, or REFUSED with a code and a byte offset (the owner's ruling: the same code and the same offset from every reader). The offset is the index of the first byte at which the input stops being the beginning of any document (or payload) of the language, or the input's length if it ended where one could still continue: it is a property of the language and the bytes, and no reader owns it. The code says what was being read there: READER-TRUNCATED (the input ended); READER-TRAILING (the object is complete and this byte may not follow it); READER-DEPTH (this bracket or brace would open an eighth level); READER-DUPLICATE (this closing quote completes a name the object already has); READER-STRING (inside a string: a control character, an escape that is not the language's, ill-formed UTF-8); READER-NUMBER (inside an integer, or a digit or one of . e E + - directly after one: a leading zero, a minus with no digit 1-9 after it, the digit that takes it out of range, a fraction, an exponent); READER-STRUCTURE (any other byte that cannot come next). The typed value of an accepted input is compared as the sha256 of its RECORD-0 canonical JSON; a member's position in an object carries no meaning. ONE RUST READER (the owner's ruling: one file, shared by path; one persisted language, one reader, many consumers): kernel/savedform.rs, beside the kernel's formats.rs, included by the shell and by the workshop's sessionwalk, session and edit. The four parsers there today — one text copied into three files, and a different one in workshop/edit.rs — are removed. The file owns reading the language and its one string spelling and nothing else: it knows nothing of the shell, the workshop, a session, admission, a renderer, a file or a process. DESIGN-EVENT-0.hypothesis: Whether a design can enter a session as one transition — DESIGN-EVENT-0, locked as the next rung by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-06, which put seven properties into one court and gave none of them a gate of its own: one proposal and one admission; a batch means its operations in order; what is admitted is the net change set; what was previewed is what is admitted; replay stays the authority; a preview is not a second world; every editor speaks the same event. His court of the same day settled the four questions the tree forced, and each answer is recorded below where it applies. ADMIT-0, READER-COURT-0, REASON-COURT-0 and MINT-WATCH-0 are not amended by this entry. THE CLAIM. A canonical batch of one to 4,096 typed operations is either refused whole, leaving nothing, or admitted by one admission as that many ordinary edit events of the session's log; and then the world, the head, the replay, the saved events and the session one steps back to are those of the same operations admitted one at a time through ADMIT-0, in the same order, from the same parent. The owner's first wording said zero-to-N operations and one ordinary session event. His court settled both: a batch of no operations is not in the language, and one design event is one admission, not one fold. WHAT A DESIGN EVENT IS (the owner's ruling, locked). The session stays an ordinary event stream. A batch of N operations is N items of the log, each an ordinary edit (cell:x,z,. or cell:x,z,# or tile:CLASS,R,G,B) made by the session's own push, with its own validation, its own witness and its own fold, so each keeps the meaning any edit has. The batch is the transaction boundary and not a new kind of event: there is no second folding rule, and the head after a batch is the head of N ordinary edits because it is N ordinary edits. All N are appended by one admission, in memory, before anything is written. The admission writes one journal and one sealed file, with the lineage of any admission: S's head and S's event count. S is never modified. Stepping back from the child is therefore stepping back over the whole batch, and no session that loads stands inside one. THE LANGUAGE is VRDNP2, a new version beside VRDNP1; VRDNP1 is not changed in any byte it accepts or refuses, and shell admit is as registered. A batch is 6 + N lines, each ended by one LF, nothing before the first and nothing after the last: VRDNP2; renderer=, bearing=, parent= and proposal=, each with 64 characters of 0-9a-f, as in VRDNP1; operations=N; then N operation lines, each one of: open X,Z; close X,Z; paint CLASS COLOUR — one space where a space is shown. N is "0" or a digit 1-9 and at most three more digits, in 1..4096. A coord, a class and a colour are VRDNP1's: a coord in 0..65535, a class one of wall0, wall1, wall2, wall3, floor, a colour in 0..16777215 read as R*65536 + G*256 + B. No other byte is legal. A batch is 322 to 74,059 bytes. WHY IT IS CANONICAL (the owner's ruling). A VRDNP2 batch denotes a net change set: a set of targets, each with the one value it is to have. So a target cannot occur twice, and an operation followed by its inverse is not in the language — not because an inverse edit is illegal (two VRDNP1 admissions may still open a cell and close it again), but because a change set has one value for each target. And a set has one spelling: the cell operations come first, in row-major order (Z ascending, then X ascending, strictly, so no cell twice, whether opened or closed), then the paints in the order wall0, wall1, wall2, wall3, floor (strictly, so no class twice). Each typed batch therefore has exactly one byte sequence: the shell's writer emits it and the recognizer accepts nothing else. Canonicalising belongs to whatever compiles a design — the design tool, a mouse, a recipe, a model — and never to the shell, which recognizes or refuses and rewrites nothing. A normal form has to be idempotent: writing the operations of a recognized batch again, in whatever order they are handed over, gives the batch's own bytes, and doing it to that output gives them again. Whether an operation changes anything depends on the parent, so it is checked at admission: an operation the session refuses, or one that leaves the world as it is, refuses the whole batch. THE SEAM. shell design --session S --proposal P, with shell admit's grant options, reads P's bytes, recognizes them or refuses them, and admits the batch to the saved session S. The checks, in this order, the first that applies: ADMIT-IO; ADMIT-SIZE (more than 74,059 bytes); ADMIT-PARSE (the first line that is not the language, and what was expected there); ADMIT-RANGE (the first line holding an integer outside its domain; a count of 0 or above 4,096 is one); ADMIT-ORDER (the first operation that does not come strictly after the one before it in the registered order); ADMIT-PREVIEW (with --previewed: the bytes' digest is not the previewed one); ADMIT-PROGRAM; the session loader's own refusals; ADMIT-SESSION; ADMIT-ANCHOR (the parent is not S's head; both are named; there is no rebase); ADMIT-DUPLICATE (the proposal id is in S's admitted history, under either language); then the operations in order, each as ADMIT-0 checks one — ADMIT-CAPABILITY (outside the grant), ADMIT-AUTHORITY (the session's own validation of the edit, or nothing to change) — the refusal naming the operation's line; and last ADMIT-PREVIEW again (with --previewed: the head reached is not the previewed one). The whole byte sequence is recognized before any integer's domain is looked at, and every domain before the order. ADMIT-ORDER and ADMIT-PREVIEW are first registered here; the others name the reasons ADMIT-0 gave them. A refused batch leaves no run directory, no journal and no file, at whichever operation it was refused, and nothing of the operations before that one exists anywhere. The grant is the admitter's, from the command line, as in ADMIT-0; a batch cannot carry one. THE ENVELOPE. Each of the N events carries the batch's envelope beside it, never in the head: ten text members — ADMIT-0's eight (language, proposal, digest, renderer, bearing, parent, head, grant) and two more, place and count. The language is VRDNP2; the proposal id and the digest of the batch's exact bytes are the batch's; parent and head are the chain's own heads before and after that event, as for any envelope; place and count are decimals with no leading zero, 1 <= place <= count <= 4096. A batch in a session is whole or the session is refused: its events stand one after another with nothing between them, place 1 to place count in order, and agree in language, proposal id, digest, renderer, bearing, grant and count. A proposal id names one admission: it stands in one batch, and in no other envelope of either language. The batch's anchor is the parent at place 1 and its result the head at place count. The shell's loader, the workshop and verify/livesession.py each hold this, and none of them reads the language: they take the envelope as typed values of the saved form. An envelope that is not VRDNP2's ten members is judged as ADMIT-0 judges any envelope, so ADMIT-0's own plant — an eight-member envelope naming VRDNP2, planted as a language that is not VRDNP1 — is refused where and as it was. PREVIEW (the owner's ruling, locked). shell design --dry-run is the projection of the admission itself: the same bytes through the same recognizer, the same checks in the same order and the same replay in memory. It prints the binding on one line — the language, the parent head, the digest of the bytes, the head the batch would give and the operation count — and writes no run directory, no journal and no session; S and every other session are as they were. A refusal is the refusal the admission would give, with the same code and the same line. That line is the binding (the owner's addition): an admission given --previewed DIGEST,HEAD refuses ADMIT-PREVIEW before anything is written unless the bytes it was given have that digest and the head it reaches is that head. The parent and the language are inside the bytes, so the digest covers them; a parent that is no longer S's head is ADMIT-ANCHOR, as ever, and never an admission against another world. An admission given no --previewed is an admission without a preview and is not refused for that. REPLAY, AND THE MEMO (the owner's ruling: full verification locked, delta verification deferred). Every admitted batch is replayed against a verified parent; unchanged witnesses may reuse their exact prior digest, but no historical computation is trusted merely because it was previously verified. So each admission still loads and replays the whole of S, and the shell still reads back and verifies the file it wrote. The one change to replay is an exact memo inside one process: the session keeps the sha256 of the level's bytes and of the tiles' bytes; a cell edit recomputes the level's and reuses the tiles', a tile edit recomputes the tiles' and reuses the level's; content is the sha256 of the two, as before. The bytes not edited are the same bytes, so the digest reused is the digest that would be computed. It is not a checkpoint, there is no new trust root, and nothing is skipped: every event of every session is still replayed. Verifying only a delta, a checkpoint that lets replay be skipped, and any trust in a seal are not in this rung, and the phrase verify the delta is not used for what this rung does. The memo changes one statement in each of the session's two edit pushes: the content computed from the level's bytes and the tiles' bytes becomes the hash of the two digests the session keeps. LIVE-INPUT-0's fence and LIVE-AUTHOR-0's fence each hold that statement by its text, as replay_from's own. Both rows are re-pinned on purpose in the build, to the memo's statements, each named in the build's commit, as earlier rungs re-pinned them; what the two rows held there — that an edit's content is the content the reference replay computes — is held from then on by this rung's replay row, against the unmemoised computation and against the workshop. No other row of an earlier rung changes its text. WHAT A DEATH LEAVES. A journal now takes N records, each put and flushed as any record is. A run ended anywhere leaves S untouched; what it left behind either loads to S's head (none of the batch is on disk), or to the child's head with every envelope intact (all of it is), or is refused by the loader (part of it is: a batch is not whole). Nothing loads to any other head. THE SEVEN PROPERTIES, AND WHERE EACH IS HELD. (1) One proposal, one admission: the admit row. (2) Batch means sequence: the same row, against ADMIT-0's own admissions one at a time, and the replay row against two independent replays. (3) Net change set: the language row holds the normal form; the netting itself is a compiler's and is content time. (4) What was previewed is what is admitted: the binding, in the admit row. (5) Replay stays the authority: the replay row, with the memo held against the unmemoised computation. (6) A preview is not a second world: the dry run writes nothing, in the admit row. (7) Every editor speaks the same event: DECLARED for editors that do not exist; what is held is that there is one batch language with one recognizer, and that the design tool, the first consumer, changes a session through it and through nothing else. THE DESIGN OF 2026-10-06. The design text the owner ran on his host (room 6,3 16,10; entrance 6,6; entrance 11,10; open 11,11; paint floor 60,70,90), compiled against the witness level from the camera 28,28,N, is 60 operations — 56 cells opened, 3 closed, 1 class painted — in row-major order and then the class, which is VRDNP2's order. Sixty ADMIT-0 admissions took the session from head 73571153c2fca1ae9412f82dff335fa134d3bc06fb785b0878a032cfa442391c to head c18a71f6af8d269095c2789b9887f160344f15bed17a88782b47e24cd77c1036 on the build container; the owner's host printed the same parent head in full and the same first twelve characters of the result. The one batch of those 60 operations has to reach that head: a value registered before the batch seam exists. THE TWO REFUSAL RUNGS. This rung changes files that REASON-COURT-0 and MINT-WATCH-0 pin, and adds its rows after theirs. Both said what that takes. The build therefore carries two amendment entries, REASON-COURT-0a and MINT-WATCH-0a, each with its own hash, naming the pinned files this rung changes with their new sha256 and (MINT-WATCH-0a) the raise sites this rung adds to verify/livesession.py, registered as sites no row before the watch reaches. Neither register's reasons, classes, rule or rows change, and no row before this rung may end or mint otherwise than it is registered to: if holding that needs more than the two amendments say here, the build stops and the owner rules. This rung's own rows run after both watches and are heard by neither. Their refusals are held this way: every non-zero ending of a child they start is one of the refusals or planted deaths this entry registers and carries its code in a code head, judged by this rung's last row with the reader of a code head that REASON-COURT-0 fixed; no statement of this rung requires a refusal without naming its code; and each forged file differs from one that verifies in one respect only. The correctness claim is equivalence. What a batch costs is measured apart from it, off the gate, and is not a registered quantity. A PROTOTYPE CAME FIRST. Its lines are the byte sequences between LFs; a CR directly before an LF is not part of the line; bytes after the last LF are a last line, and a design that ends in LF has no line after it. With the comment and the spaces and tabs at either end dropped, a line is empty or one statement: words separated by one or more spaces or tabs, every byte of a word printable ASCII (0x21 to 0x7E). The statements: open CELL; open CELL CELL; close CELL; close CELL CELL; room CELL CELL; entrance CELL; paint CLASS R,G,B. A CELL is X,Z, each "0" or a digit 1-9 and at most four more digits, and names a cell inside the parent's level. Two cells are the corners of a rectangle in either order; one cell is the rectangle of that cell. A room's rectangle is at least three cells each way. A CLASS is one of wall0, wall1, wall2, wall3, floor; R, G and B are each "0" or a digit 1-9 and at most two more digits, at most 255. A design holds at least one statement and at most 64. This is narrower than what the tool happened to accept (it split on every blank Python knows and took a CR anywhere): the pin is deliberate, and the statements are the tool's. WHAT A DESIGN MEANS. The statements are applied in order to a copy of the parent's world: open writes floor to every cell of its rectangle, close writes rock, room writes rock to the rectangle's rim and floor to its inside, entrance writes floor to its cell, paint gives a class one colour; a later statement writes over an earlier one. A rectangle is written row by row, each row from its lower X. The world that results is the design's TARGET. The design's change set is the net difference between the parent's world and the target: for each cell whose value differs, open if the target holds floor and close if it holds rock, the cells in row-major order (Z, then X); then, for each class a statement painted, in the order wall0, wall1, wall2, wall3, floor, whose colour is not the one colour the parent's class already wholly has, paint. That is VRDNP2's own order, so the change set has one byte form and the compiler writes it; the admission still rewrites nothing. A statement that writes what is already there, and a paint of the colour a class wholly has, add nothing. A room is a statement and so is an entrance: once compiled there are operations, and once admitted there are ordinary edits, and nothing in a batch, an envelope or a session names a room. WHAT A DESIGN MAY NOT SAY (the refusal boundary). Three rules are the source language's and are checked where a statement writes: a statement may not write floor to a cell on the level's border (COMPILE-BORDER, the statement's line); a statement may not write to a stair cell (COMPILE-STAIR, the statement's line; VRDNP2 opens and closes and has no stair, so a design over one is refused and never rounded to floor or rock); and the target may not leave the camera's cell closed (COMPILE-CAMERA). A design whose change set is empty is refused (COMPILE-EMPTY): a VRDNP2 batch has at least one operation, and the compiler does not write one that says nothing. A change set of more than 4,096 operations is refused (COMPILE-SIZE). The compiler never emits part of a design, never skips a statement it cannot honour, and never clips a rectangle. THE COMMAND. shell design-compile --session S --design D reads D's bytes and the saved session S, and writes the batch's bytes, and nothing else, to standard output, ending 0; or refuses, ending 2 with nothing on standard output. It writes no batch file, no journal and no session, makes no run directory, and leaves S as it was. As every command of the shell does, the run puts its one line in the run ledger and a refusal puts its one record in the refusal log; the compiler writes nothing else. The checks, in this order, the first that applies: COMPILE-IO (D cannot be read); COMPILE-SIZE (D is more than 16,384 bytes); the session loader's own refusals; COMPILE-SESSION (S is a journal and not a saved session); then D's lines in order, the first line that fails; within a line the statement's shape first (its verb and the number of its words), then its cells from left to right, then a room's size — COMPILE-PARSE (the line is not the language), COMPILE-RANGE (a cell outside the level, or a room smaller than three cells each way), COMPILE-SIZE (a statement after the 64th); a design with no statement is COMPILE-PARSE at its last line; then the statements in order, each cell as it is written — COMPILE-BORDER, then COMPILE-STAIR; then COMPILE-CAMERA; then COMPILE-SIZE (the operations); then COMPILE-EMPTY. Every line is read as the language before any statement is applied. COMPILE-PARSE, COMPILE-RANGE, COMPILE-BORDER, COMPILE-STAIR and a statement's COMPILE-SIZE name the design's line; the others name none. The nine codes are first registered here. THE BATCH it writes is VRDNP2 as DESIGN-EVENT-0 registered it: renderer= and bearing= are the compiling shell's own identities, parent= is S's head, proposal= is the design's id, operations=N and the N operations of the change set. Nothing in it depends on a clock, a host, a path or a random value: the same design bytes and the same session give the same bytes on every run. THE ID (his ruling, locked): proposal_id = H(exact design bytes) — the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 of D's bytes exactly as they were read, with nothing normalised: a design saved with CR LF, with another comment or with one more space is another design with another id, though it may compile to the same operations. The chain is then: exact design bytes, design digest, proposal id, admission envelope, ordinary session events. DESIGN-EVENT-0 already puts the proposal id beside every event a batch admits and seals it with the session, so no member is added to the saved form and READER-COURT-0 is not reopened. The id is a commitment and not a copy: the design cannot be recovered from it, and it is provenance only for whoever holds the bytes. The design tool keeps them, by id, in the project. This establishes what source produced a change, not why the world should contain it; and no operation is attributed to a statement, which he ruled a separate requirement. One consequence is the session's own rule and not a new one: a session refuses a proposal id already in its admitted history, so the same design bytes are admitted at most once in a history, and a design to be admitted again differs in a byte. THE ADMISSION IS NOT THE COMPILER'S COURT. shell design takes a batch and never a design; shell design-compile writes no session. The preview is still the dry run of the batch, and the binding is still DESIGN-EVENT-0's. A batch the compiler writes can still be refused by the admission: for its anchor, its id, the grant, or the session's own validation. WHAT THIS DOES TO DESIGN-EVENT-0'S WORDS. That entry says canonicalising belongs to whatever compiles a design and never to the shell, which recognizes or refuses and rewrites nothing. The sentence is about the admission, and it stands as a statement about the admission: shell design recognizes or refuses and rewrites nothing. His ruling in that court was that canonicalising belongs in the design compiler and not in the authority or session layer; his ruling in this one places the compiler in the shell's program as a command apart from the admission. The compiler writes a batch from a design. It is handed no batch and reorders, nets and rewrites none. NO VERIFIER RECONSTRUCTS. The shell's loader, the workshop and the sealer read no design, call no compiler and write no batch; nothing rebuilds a proposal's bytes from admitted events. The owner's deferral of that (2026-10-06) stands. The gate's reference writes the batch it expects from a design and a parent, in its own rows, and from nothing else. OUT, BY NAME (his ruling): readings stay the design tool's own views and are not certified; constraints get their own court; no status beyond those is defined. Persistent objects are a later rung. WHAT WAS SEEN BEFORE THIS REGISTRATION, disclosed. The shell's compiler does not exist. A reference compiler was written in Python from the description above and run against the shell as built, through its admission. The registered design below compiled to 60 operations and a batch of 908 bytes, and the existing dry run gave c18a71f6af8d269095c2789b9887f160344f15bed17a88782b47e24cd77c1036 for it; so the id, the digest and the target's content registered below were computed before the compiler exists, and the head predates both. Ten planted behaviours were tried the same way — seven as planted variants of the reference, three as the batches a compiler that approximates would write — and three things were found that shape the court. One: a plant bites only on some designs and parents — the short rectangle gives the honest bytes on the registered design, because the column it leaves out was rock already; and on a parent with a history a net taken against the base world restates the parent's own edits, which the admission refuses itself (nothing to change), unless the design undoes the whole of that history. Two: the admission admits a batch that closes the camera's cell, and a batch that opens a stair. Those two rules are the source language's alone. Three: the same design bytes offered a second time in one history are refused ADMIT-DUPLICATE, and with one more comment line are admitted.

HERMENEUTICS-0.hypothesis: Whether the meaning of the design language can be fixed apart from the two programs that compile it — HERMENEUTICS-0, named by the owner on 2026-10-07 for the gap DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0's own amendment states: a misreading of a statement shared by the compiler and the reference is caught by neither of that rung's equalities, because its target is taken by the gate's own reading. His question: what is the authoritative meaning of VERDANDI-DESIGN 0, independently of either compiler. His definition: a registered adjudication of the denotation of the source language — not what a designer probably meant. His ruling on its place: lock the concept now, defer its build until after DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0, reject folding it into that rung or treating the agreement of the compiler and the reference as evidence of meaning. A later text of his asked that it be registered only as a corpus that can redden, with the semantic laws beside it, and not as an empty rung. This entry is that. DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0 (2baa42f3) and DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0a (c414587d) are not amended by it, and it is not a dependency of their build. THE COURT (2026-10-07). Six readings that DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0 had decided by inheriting them from the design tool were put to him as cases on the registered parent, each with the readings on the table drawn as small grids. Case 1 he ruled himself: as registered. For the others he first asked for the wisest path from the literature, and on two expressed no preference; he was then given one reading that covers all six, with a recommendation for each case, and ratified it: the reading, a LOCK on all five remaining cases as registered, the four laws as theorems, and a corpus of the six cases and three more. So one case is his own ruling and five are his ratification of a recommendation, and the entry says which. THE READING HE RATIFIED. A statement denotes a finite partial map from targets to values, the same on every parent. The targets are the cells of the level and the five classes; a cell's value is floor or rock, a class's value is a colour. open R gives floor to every cell of the rectangle R; close R gives rock; room R gives rock to the cells on R's rim and floor to the cells inside it; entrance C gives floor to the one cell C; paint K V gives the class K the colour V. A design denotes its statements' maps composed in line order, the later winning: where two statements name the same target, the design's map has the later one's value. The design's target on a parent is the parent with that map laid over it: every target the map names has the map's value, and everything else, the stairs among it, is the parent's. The change set is the targets whose value in the map is not the parent's, and VRDNP2 encodes exactly that: the net change set is an encoding of a difference and not part of the meaning. Two guards belong to the language. The static guard: no statement may give a frozen cell a value other than its own. A cell on the level's border is frozen at rock, so a statement may give it rock and nothing else; a stair is frozen at itself, and the language has no value for a stair, so no statement may name a stair cell. It is judged statement by statement in line order, whether or not a later statement names the cell again. The state guard: the target may not leave the camera's cell closed. It is judged once, on the target. And one limit is the encoding's and not the meaning's: a design whose change set is empty has a meaning, its target is its parent, and has no batch, because a batch holds at least one operation; COMPILE-EMPTY is the compiler saying it has nothing to write. This reading says in other words what DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0's entry says in prose. It is ratified as the same meaning and creates no successor language. If the two are ever found to differ, that entry is not edited: the difference is a finding, and the owner rules it. THE RULINGS. Each is LOCK, and the other readings put to him are not supported. Case 1, where the rules are judged: the border and the stair where a statement writes, the camera on the target — his own ruling; rejected: all three on the target; all three where a statement writes. Case 2, open on a stair: refused, because a stair is frozen; rejected: a no-op because a stair is walkable already, which would make open the one statement whose meaning depends on what was there; and the stair becoming floor, which would let a design destroy what no design can restore. Case 3, entrance: one opened cell, open under another name; rejected for this language: an entrance that must join floor, which is a relation between spaces and belongs to a court of constraints. Case 4, room: the rim rock and the inside floor, whatever was there, so floor already on the rim is closed; rejected: a rim that keeps its openings, which would depend on what was there. Case 5, paint: the whole class one colour; rejected: a blend with what was there. Case 6, a design that changes nothing: refused by the compiler, with its meaning intact; rejected: an accepted compile that writes nothing. No case was found underspecified, and none is deferred. THE CORPUS. Ten designs on one parent, the registered parent of DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0: the session of head 73571153c2fca1ae9412f82dff335fa134d3bc06fb785b0878a032cfa442391c, the witness level of 48 by 32 cells, the camera at 28,28. Each design is the line VERDANDI-DESIGN 0 and the statements given here, every line ended by one LF. Its semantic target is literal: the cells that change and what they become, or the refusal with its code and line. The targets were typed by hand from the rulings and the parent's cells, and were produced by neither program. They are: H1a — close 28,28 / open 28,28 / close 27,28 — TARGET: rock at 27,28; no other cell and no class changes; H1b — open 0,27 / close 0,27 / close 27,28 — REFUSED: COMPILE-BORDER at line 2; H2 — open 7,26 / close 27,28 — REFUSED: COMPILE-STAIR at line 2; H2' — close 34,28 — REFUSED: COMPILE-STAIR at line 2; H3 — entrance 40,29 — TARGET: floor at 40,29; nothing else changes; H3' — entrance 11,24 — TARGET: floor at 11,24; nothing else changes; H4 — room 20,24 26,28 — TARGET: rock at 21,24 22,24 23,24 24,24 25,24 20,26 26,26 20,28 21,28 22,28 23,28 24,28 25,28 26,28 (fourteen cells); no cell becomes floor; nothing else changes; H4' — room 38,2 42,6 — TARGET: floor at 39,3 40,3 41,3 39,4 40,4 41,4 39,5 40,5 41,5 (nine cells); no cell becomes rock; nothing else changes; H5 — paint floor 60,70,90 — TARGET: the class floor is the colour 60,70,90 throughout; no cell changes; H6 — open 40,29 / close 40,29 — TARGET: the parent itself, nothing changes; and so the compiler's answer is REFUSED: COMPILE-EMPTY. H1a and H1b are Case 1; H2 is Case 2; H3 Case 3; H4 Case 4; H5 Case 5; H6 Case 6; H2', H3' and H4' are the three added. WHAT EITHER PROGRAM HAD ALREADY SHOWN, said plainly, because the fence below is only as good as this. No compiler exists in the shell. The gate's reference exists, and before this court H1a, H1b, H2 and H3 had been run through it exactly and their outcomes read, and the paint of H5 and a net-zero design like H6 had been run in other designs. H4 and H4' were passed through it inside a check of the laws, where only the equality of two spellings was looked at and no target was printed or read. H2' and H3' were never run. So the court was not blind to the reference in four of the ten, and the entry does not claim otherwise. THE LAWS, each a theorem of the reading and ratified by him as a property of the language, each with its condition. Corner order: for open, close and room, a rectangle given by two opposite corners in any of the four ways denotes the same map. Fixed point: if a design is not refused on a parent and has the target T, then on a parent whose world is T no guard refuses it and its target is T; its change set there is empty, so the compiler's answer there is COMPILE-EMPTY — the denotation is unchanged, and recompiling is not an accepted no-op. Room: room A B, and close A B followed by open of the rectangle one cell inside it, denote the same map; so on every parent they have the same target, and a guard refuses one exactly when it refuses the other, though the line named may differ. Exchange: two adjacent statements whose maps agree on every target both name — two that name no target in common among them — may be exchanged, and the design denotes the same map; whether the design is refused does not change, though the line named, and the code where both are refused by the static guard for different reasons, may. No law is claimed for two statements that disagree on a target both name: there the later wins, and exchanging them changes the map. THE INDEPENDENCE FENCE (his). Semantic targets are fixed without consulting the production compiler or its reference's output. The targets are data in this entry. At the build the gate makes each target's bytes from these literal cells and the parent's bytes, calling neither program, and holds both programs to them. The central predicate is Meaning_court(D,S) = Target_owner(D,S), and never Meaning_court(D,S) = Compile_shell(D,S). THE PLANTS are the ones a comparison of the two programs cannot see: each is planted alike in the shell's compiler and in the gate's reference, so that their bytes agree. Five, by his list: a room whose rim keeps its openings; a first statement that wins over a later one; a rectangle whose corners are taken in one order only; an entrance that writes nothing; and a paint of a class's own colour, or a net-zero design, written as operations. Each has to be caught by a named case of the corpus or a named law. Read against DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0 before this entry was committed, that rung is less blind than a comparison alone: it registered the values of one design, computed before any plant, and its amendment registered outcomes in words, and each of these five plants appears to change something registered there. So this entry does not claim that a plant is caught here alone. For each plant the build records which rows of either rung catch it, and if that rung's rows catch all five, the row says so: that is a finding about how much its registered values already fix, and not a failure of this court. What this court adds is not a catch no other row makes; it is that the six readings are adjudicated and their targets are the owner's and not a program's. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH (his list): compiler correctness; VRDNP2 correctness; admission correctness; authority legality; designer intent; completeness of the language. SEMIOTICS is not in this rung. By his second text it is a vocabulary audit one level earlier, declared and not registered. The court leaves it three notes: entrance promises a relation that its write does not check; room is a statement and not an object; paint replaces and does not tint. THE OUTSIDE READING behind the recommendation, attributed and not claimed: the lens laws of bidirectional programming (GetPut, PutPut) for writes that compose; SQL's immediate and deferred constraints for the two levels of Case 1; patch theory for when changes commute; RFC 9413 on tolerating unexpected input for refusing rather than guessing; a dungeon generator's connectors for a door as a relation; Git's refusal of an empty commit for Case 6. They were opened on 2026-10-07. They shaped the recommendation, and nothing in this entry rests on them. WHEN IT IS BUILT (his order): after DESIGN-IR/DIFF-0 is built, its court run and its gate FULL×2. Not before.

It is a real defect of the gate and not of the tree: the row is establishing a property of what was written about a refusal, and its way of observing was accidentally broader than the property.
